GARD-inspired Flow Lenia synthesis · research synthesis · 30 Aug 2026

Write Access Falls While Sibling Forms Keep Diverging

Flow Lenia is a continuous, multichannel field that can reorganize into temporally consistent, coherent individuals. We asked when its future first becomes constrained as an individual, and how that constraint changes what interventions can do. We compared prospective forecasting, exact future fans, closed-loop controls, releases, and hidden-composition transplants. Across them, the organism appears in possibility space before silhouette; development then makes it harder to rewrite without forcing siblings toward one shape.

fresh prospective frozen direct held-out protocol correction post-hoc descriptive
The short answer constraint · address · hardening

A pre-form state constrains futures and already carries a response address; aging makes it harder to write; feedback still moves targets, but the whole policy’s comparative edge reverses after release.

01

Interventions distinguish early states.

At passage 8 the action-world is already as separated as at passage 32, and a whole-over-parts signal rises before sustained visible structure.

02

The response already distinguishes its source.

A specimen-or-genotype-specific response is re-identifiable across the earliest interval tested, passage 12→24. Its onset is left-censored.

03

Commitment is selective.

Timing and spatial leverage harden while sibling shape spread widens. Rigidity is not convergence.

01 · the instrument

A body is more than a picture.

Flow Lenia is a continuous, multichannel field. We ask whether its present state constrains its future as a coordinated whole, how interventions reshape that future, and whether the response later becomes individually recognizable.

The whole-over-parts instrument compares how well the full state forecasts its next state with the strongest tested separable split. A positive change means the whole is catching up with that split. It is not IIT Φ, and in the prospective precursor the absolute whole-minus-sum level remains negative: the best split still forecasts better at every phase.

The campaign therefore does not rest on a single score. It triangulates information, direct interventions, held-out releases, exact visible-state controls, and hidden-composition transplants.

Future fan

One state, many exact continuations

Run matched interventions or noise futures from the same checkpoint and measure how far their outcomes spread.

Visible / hidden

Same body, different composition

The visible field sums channels. Different channel mixtures can be exactly invisible in that sum while changing later response.

Frozen / post-hoc

Decision before data / map after data

Frozen tests answer predeclared questions. Post-hoc panels are valuable for mechanism and next experiments, but do not inherit that status.

02 · before the silhouette

The future is organized before the body is obvious.

Two early facts arrive by different routes: the fresh prospective whole-over-parts relation rises, while a fixed-age descriptive assay finds alternative-action futures already richly separated at passage 8.

prospective whole−sum rise+0.364

95% interval +0.231 to +0.502; 39/54 eligible windows and 15/16 family means positive. This is catch-up, about 4% of the whole-state ~8.76 nats—not whole-state dominance.

held-out event prediction+0.00043 AUC

Controls move from 0.8089 to 0.8093 when whole−sum is added. Specific event prediction is unresolved.

prospective repertoireρ = −0.248

Whole−sum predicts a narrower future timing range after checkpoint, shape, topology, size, and raw-change controls; interval −0.420 to −0.045.

fixed passage 8 action-world104.4%

Future-history separation at passage 8 is 104.4% of passage 32 across 39 organisms and 5,616 futures.

Retrospective atlas, kept separate from the prospective result: event-aligned whole-over-parts moves from −1.75 early to −0.32 at transition, a +1.43 rise in all 16 families. It shows where to look, not a future-blind forecast.
What the null taught uscoordinate, not lever

Past-only geometry tracked developmental progress—39 of 62 trajectories were strictly monotone—but adding it did not improve held-out countdown error (39.88 steps with ordinary controls, 40.46 with geometry). Direct Φ-high versus Φ-low intervention effects also changed sign with phase.

The information geometry was useful as a coordinate. It was not a universal button that advanced development.

03 · selective closure

Commitment does not mean one final shape.

The system loses particular degrees of freedom on different schedules: timing futures contract, spatial interventions lose leverage, and action meanings become less context-sensitive. Other degrees remain open.

future timing repertoireρ = −0.248

Higher prospective whole−sum predicts less timing spread across nine matched futures. Fresh, future-blind cohort.

gate release memory+0.075

Cumulative open-minus-closed causal-history distance after release; interval +0.059 to +0.090, 16/16 family directions.

spatial leverage+0.00290

Turn minus two passages later; interval +0.00049 to +0.00529. The predeclared four-passage persistence rule failed.

action grammar rewrite+0.002935

Before-turn minus after-turn context rewrite; interval +0.000493 to +0.005409 across 19 families.

Timing closes

Future event times become less variable.

The strongest prospective relation is to timing-range contraction. A direct nested branching primary on timing itself was null; a predeclared fine-field secondary shifted by roughly 2.3%.

Spatial leverage closes

Where matter sits matters from the beginning.

Scrambling the same cells while preserving genotype, mass, composition, and world slows formation by 12.85, 22.51, and 30.59 passages at successively finer scrambling scales.

Action grammar hardens

The meaning of a second action becomes harder to rewrite.

The six-edge geometry of second-action outcomes changes less across first-action contexts after the turn.

Shape stays plural

Siblings fan outward instead of converging.

Initialization-perturbed width grows from 0.032 at age 60 to 0.079 at age 900. “Commitment” is individuation plus rigidity, not convergence.

Exact visible-state controlthe picture is not the state

Across 156 transplant starts, visible fields were bit-for-bit identical while hidden channel composition differed. The frozen donor-axis primary was null, +0.050 [−0.258,+0.370], and hybrids were farther from donor than host in all 16 families. Yet a predeclared secondary followed 27.9% of the donor’s natural growth direction [12.1%,47.2%], 14/16 families, with strong directional asymmetry.

A fresh older-composition ignition test did not shift the developmental clock. A separate post-hoc counterweight found hidden displacement restrained later radius, −0.096 [−0.156,−0.043]. Together: hidden composition changes futures, but not as a simple donor identity or older-state clock. frozen posthoc

04 · direct adjudication

The shape result opened a better distinction.

Four sibling tests turned one narrow “fine-shape closure” story into a richer one: push susceptibility falls with age, but siblings do not converge and a fresh confirmation cannot resolve the original tiny shape effect.

Status of the original lead

Interesting secondary, not settled closure.

The earlier −0.00399 fine-shape result was one predeclared secondary contrast, but its structural-peak timing arm was selected post-hoc and only 5 of 78 predeclared contrasts resolved. The fresh 12-family experiment made that shape contrast its sole primary and returned an interval crossing zero.

fine shape sole primary−0.0019

Interval −0.0076 to +0.0038; six families each direction; no arm contrast separates from zero. The earlier −0.0040 remains within what 12 families could miss.

steerability prediction+0.00385

Pre-turn pushes move later futures more than post-turn pushes; interval +0.00185 to +0.00545, 15/16 families. Push divergence falls about 69% with age.

basin-width prediction−0.0378

The frozen prediction expected positive early-minus-late width. Every family goes the other way.

history primary+0.0066

Matched-present future-distance ratio does not rise cleanly. A separate pre-named lookalike count collapses 6,144→1,665 with ρ −0.988.

Resolution: rigidity ≠ sibling convergence. A body can become harder to rewrite while its population occupies a wider set of mature forms.
05 · developmental causal impedance

The same write produces less future change as the body ages.

Across 64 organisms, 16 groups, 19 ages, and 7,296 futures, fixed writes retain the same affected-matter fraction yet lose downstream leverage. This is development-wide damping, not an information-turn-locked transition.

fixed .12 · D4−0.001875

Late minus early difference; interval −0.002155 to −0.001579, all 16 families.

physical write~40% smaller

Realized matter L1 falls 56.94→34.18, but D4 per physical write still falls to factor 0.0799 [0.0661,0.0969].

approximate match51.5%

Only 1,880 of 3,648 selected matches lie within 25% of target; early dose-floor fallback was used in 401/768.

common supportpost-hoc survives

On common support, D120 and D240 damping remain −0.00461 and −0.00889, all 16 families.

06 · the controller tournament

Whole-state feedback reaches the target. It does not earn a unique edge.

The corrected frozen comparator includes sham, replay, and the strongest local controller per instance. Under that protocol, active whole-state achievement survives; whole-over-best advantage and developmental gain do not.

Protocol-conformant correction

The original joint “pass” is superseded.

The frozen plan included sham=0 in the maximum comparator. The original analysis omitted it. Corrected result SHA 4b30ab79… replaces the original result SHA 25e2802b… for every joint-decision claim.

whole vs sham+4.2318

Interval +3.4167 to +5.0271; 16/16 family directions. Active achievement survives correction.

whole advantage+0.3857

Interval -0.6762 to +1.2916; strongest per-instance sham/replay/local comparator. Null.

developmental gain+0.6330

Interval -0.5633 to +1.6612. Null.

held-out +128-6.5831

Interval -11.2502 to -2.7983; 12/16 families negative. The advantage reverses after release.

Resolution: active steerability ≠ unique whole-observer advantage. The policy can do real work while equally resourced restricted policies remain competitive—and while its advantage disappears after release.
07 · causal individuality

The response already carries an address at the first interval tested.

A response fingerprint can re-identify the source specimen across development after removing the linear component of 17 predefined passive summaries. Because each specimen has a unique genotype, the safe claim is specimen-or-genotype-specific.

Operational resultOnset is left-censored at passage 12→24.

Identity is already detectable across the earliest tested interval. The experiment does not locate a birth between passage 12 and passage 24, and it does not separate specimen from genotype.

earliest pooled visible12 / 72

Top-1 retrieval versus frozen 99% permutation threshold 7/72; residual margin +0.23063 [0.18599,0.27062].

strict quartet43 / 72

Within same source quartet, margin +0.19440. The signal is not merely broad group separation. Post-hoc.

hidden response33 / 72

Hidden-composition fingerprint is strong; strict-quartet retrieval reaches 63/72. Post-hoc.

long horizont128 passes

t8 and t32 fail; field response passes while scalar-only response does not. This maps where the address lives. Post-hoc.

07b · documented map

The response fingerprint depends on spatial detail and observation time.

These panels replay existing receipts only. They are explicitly post-hoc and identify the next frozen discriminators; they do not change the frozen passport decision.

The stored primary was reproduced exactly.

The earliest passport survives a closer neighborhood.

0.194

hidden response

Hidden composition carries a strong address too.

0.237

Across 432 hidden-response features, passage 12→passage 24 top-1 is 45.8% and within-quartet top-1 is 87.5%. This still cannot separate specimen identity from genotype because every specimen has a unique genotype.

pooled vs split · passage 48→passage 64

The late address is crowded, not erased.

6.9% pooled

Pooled visible top-1 falls below its 8.3% null bound, yet the strict within-quartet margin is 0.236, within-quartet top-1 is 56.9%, and hidden top-1 remains 36.1%. This is pooled-visible address reorganization and crowding, not loss of individuality.

transplant sensitivity

Re-encoding perturbs the host; donor alignment adds no specific transfer.

−0.025 · +0.023

Aligned-near minus phase-scrambled donor-axis projection at passage 24 and passage 48. Both intervals cross zero. Near-donor host-response distance exceeds self re-encode by 40.23 at passage 24 and 21.64 at passage 48, showing disruption without donor-passport specificity.

Resolution: hidden composition influences futures ≠ a portable donor identity. The current design has no same-genotype donor control and cannot separate specimen history from genotype.
08 · what the whole campaign says

The experiments separate shape, responsiveness, and history.

The combined evidence supports a developmental causal individual—not a unique final morphology, a magic Φ lever, or an autonomous replicator.

Possibility

Constraint appears before silhouette.

A pre-form state already supports a structured action-world and a prospective whole-over-parts rise. The informative object is the space of possible continuations, not only the current image.

Commitment

Degrees of freedom close on different schedules.

Timing, spatial leverage, and action-context rewrite harden. Sibling basins widen, so commitment is selective closure within plural morphology.

Control

Steering is real; the comparative edge is temporary.

Feedback moves target scores during the active window. It gains no corrected unique whole-state advantage, and the comparative whole-policy advantage reverses after release.

Individuality

Response becomes re-identifiable.

By the earliest tested interval, a distributed causal response predicts specimen-or-genotype across time beyond 17 linear passive summaries.

Not claimed

No autonomous self-replication result

These are developmental organisms and exact intervention assays, not a demonstration of endogenous replication.

Not claimed

No genotype-independent passport

Specimen and genotype are confounded; the transplant fails a donor-specific transfer contrast.

Not claimed

No single universal commitment event

Information, morphology, impedance, action grammar, and retrieval have related but non-identical clocks.

09 · the next large swings

Now we can ask whether the address is learned, portable, and generative.

The next experiments should discriminate mechanisms that the present corpus has made separable—not just rerun the same tiny contrasts with more seeds.

Same-genotype lives

Separate biography from genome.

Generate multiple independent developmental histories from the same genotype, then ask whether passports retrieve genotype, individual trajectory, or both.

Closed-loop release ecology

Discover self-maintaining control regimes.

Vary duration, dose, and feedback memory across the impedance curve; freeze whether any regime persists after release rather than merely leaving a divergent scar.

Passport surgery

Locate a minimal causal address.

Use exact hidden-channel swaps, spatially tiled transplants, and horizon-selective probes to distinguish distributed composition from localized response syntax.

Reproduction and inheritance

Ask whether an address survives fission.

Track causal passports across endogenous splitting or replication-like events: which response dimensions are inherited, recombined, or rebuilt?
